title: Sledding in Berlin - Quick Summary
kicker: WALK OF BERLIN • LIVING IN BERLIN
items: **5 cm is a thin run, 10 cm is a proper day** (my thresholds). Over 31 winters, **22 had a weekend day with 5 cm or more**, but only **9 had one with 10 cm**.
**The typical winter gives 2 weekend days at 5 cm and none at 10 cm.** The last five winters gave 0, 0, 2, 3 and 3 weekend days at 5 cm.
**Snow does not wait.** The median spell of 5 cm or more lasted **3 days**, and 46 per cent lasted two days or less. Most good weekend days fall in **January and February**.

**Hills:** Teufelsberg (120 m, long and fast, old run closed and partly fenced), the Insulaner (78 m), the Kleiner Bunkerberg in Friedrichshain, and the flatter run-out in Volkspark Prenzlauer Berg for small children.
**No hill is groomed.** Mitte said in 2021 that it no longer designates sledding runs in its parks. Check the run-out before the first slide.
**My move:** go on the first morning with 5 cm or more, take the flatter hill with small children, and use the snow-odds tool in this post to test your own threshold.
